explanation.in_plain_words: Lightning Bolt is a spell you cast by paying one red mana. When you play it, you deal 3 damage to a target of your choice — this can be a creature on the battlefield or a player. It is one of the simplest and most direct damage spells in the game.
explanation.when_you_can_play_it: Because it is an Instant, you can play Lightning Bolt at almost any time — on your own turn, on your opponent's turn, or even in response to something else happening. You just need to have one red mana available to pay for it.
how_it_works: Choose a target: pick any creature on the battlefield, or pick any player (including yourself, though you usually wouldn't).
Pay the cost: spend one red mana from your lands.
The card resolves: Lightning Bolt deals exactly 3 damage to the target you chose.
If the target was a creature and it now has damage equal to or greater than its toughness, that creature dies. If the target was a player and they reach 0 life, they lose the game.
Lightning Bolt then goes to your graveyard (your discard pile).

words_to_know.definition: A type of card you can play at almost any time, even when it is not your turn. After it does its thing, it goes to your graveyard.
This is the mana cost. It means you must spend exactly one red mana to cast this card. Red mana comes from lands that produce red mana, like a Mountain.
A way of hurting a creature or player. If a creature takes damage equal to or more than its toughness (its bottom number), it dies. If a player takes damage that brings them to 0 life, they lose.
You get to freely choose what the damage hits — it can be any creature on the battlefield, or any player in the game.

explanation.example_turn: Your opponent has a creature with 2 toughness blocking your attack. On your turn, you tap a Mountain to get one red mana and play Lightning Bolt. You point it at that creature. It deals 3 damage — more than the creature's toughness — so the creature dies, and Lightning Bolt goes to your graveyard.
